item: On Windows a merge the timeout killed is rolled back fully once no git process runs (bounded wait, 120 s); a git still running past the bound leaves everything as it is and says so
summary: Killing Git for Windows' cmd\git.exe wrapper can leave the real git running and holding .git/index.lock; the helper used to say rollback_incomplete with a half-written tree. Now it waits up to LOCK_RELEASE_WAIT_S (measured basis in the code) until NO git process runs on the machine (psutil; a lock gone is not enough, since an ff merge lets it go before it moves HEAD), then resets to the old commit (also when that git finished and moved HEAD), removing a lock left behind as stale; while any git runs or that cannot be told, nothing is touched. Release line: On Windows, an update interrupted by its time limit is now rolled back fully when git releases its lock.
